subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared connected-Control-UI notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and should cron snooze/reschedule mutate the original job or create one-shot follow-up jobs?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the durable boundary affects Control UI architecture, cron scheduling semantics, context UX, security/admin notification overlap, and related webchat action issues.

options.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
options.body: Add a single Control UI notification/action model and then implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Webchat Actions
options.body: Use the broader webchat inline button/callback direction so chat, cron, and notification actions share one callback path.

options.title: Defer Popups
options.body: Keep existing inline context warnings, cron history, and Web Push settings until a larger notification roadmap is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
recommendation.body: Add a single Control UI notification/action model and then implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing signal across cron gateway behavior, notification delivery, and the previous product review for this issue.
